features: A BUILDING THAT IS ALREADY SET UP, SO YOU CAN SEE WHAT THE PROGRAM DOES — ⚠️ This version touches the database: a migration adds a column to buildings to mark the demonstration one. It does not modify any existing building.

THE PROBLEM: anyone installing KondoManager faces an empty program, and an empty program tells you nothing about what it can do. Seeing it at work meant entering units, people, thousandths, a budget and an instalment plan by hand — an hour of work before you could judge whether the software suits you.

THERE IS NOW A BUTTON ON THE BUILDINGS PAGE, next to «create building», that builds a complete building with realistic data. A dialog explains first what is about to happen, so nobody ends up with one they did not ask for.

WHAT IT CONTAINS: four units with owners, one tenant and two co-owners; the thousandths tables, including the roof terrace split under art. 1126 of the Italian Civil Code — one third to whoever has exclusive use and two thirds to everyone else, across two tables linked to the same expense; the budget, one item of which is split between owner and tenant; the instalment plan generated by the real engine and already issued; two payments, one of them partial, leaving arrears to look at; a supplier invoice with withholding tax and an offset credit note, so that less leaves the bank than the debt being closed; and a transfer that funds the works reserve.

AND THE THINGS THAT GO WRONG, because those are what a manager needs to know the program handles: an invoice over budget, awaiting ratification and visible in the chart of accounts; an unforeseen expense the budget did not contain — it creates its own item and calls for new instalments, and it is the amber section of the dashboard; a reversal, a cancelled payment with its opposite entry, because in accounting you do not delete, you correct; the F24 schedule already calculated, with the withholding ready to pay; and the operational Inbox filled in, with its tasks and the links to carry them out.

IT CAN BE REMOVED, AND THAT IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS. A building with accounting entries normally cannot be deleted — that is a deliberate protection, accounting must not vanish at the press of a button. The demonstration building is the one exception, for a precise reason: those entries were written by the program, not by a manager. Removal asks for confirmation, says what it is about to delete, and takes everything with it: the entries, the people it added to the address book and the example suppliers — but only those that no longer belong to any other building and have no user account attached, because the supplier and people lists are shared.
ONE AT A TIME: when a demonstration building already exists, the button is replaced by a red one to remove it, and the building can also be deleted from the actions menu in the list.

AND THE ERROR MESSAGE ON REAL BUILDINGS NOW SAYS WHY. Trying to delete a building with accounting entries showed only «an error occurred during deletion»: you could not tell whether it was a fault or a rule, nor that retrying was pointless. The message now says that the building has payments, F24 forms or cash accounts recorded and therefore cannot be deleted, because deleting it would throw away its accounting.

UNDER THE BONNET, THE CHOICE THAT KEEPS THIS WORK USEFUL OVER TIME: the demonstration building is not written straight into the database but built through the same doors a manager uses — the invoice service, the payments one, the instalment plan generator, the collection, the transfer, the issuing of instalments. It means it cannot produce situations the program cannot produce, and that it updates itself when the program changes. Building it this way surfaced the points where writing by hand would have produced a fake building: an expense item without its accounting anchor cannot be invoiced, the invoice service requires the payment method, an instalment plan must declare which items it covers — without that the dashboard reports it as misaligned and the demo would open with a red alarm — and instalments are not issued by changing a status, because issuing is what writes the debts owed by the owners. Seventeen automated tests now require that the building be built without a single warning, that the dashboard find it aligned, that it be removed without leaving anything behind, not even behind the link tables, that a second demo can be created after the first, and that removal refuse to touch a real building.
